output.title: Spot proof-of-concept debt before you call the pilot done
output.body:
If you run a small business, proof-of-concept debt is the work you quietly defer during a pilot: missing documentation, an untested edge case, a brittle manual step, or a bug you decide can wait until later. The mistake is not the deferment itself. It is treating every deferred item as if it belongs in the same bucket.

Use one simple owner decision at the end of the pilot: is this still a one-off proof, or has it turned into something you now need to extend into production? If it is only a proof, keep the deferred items in a separate post-pilot list. If it is now a production candidate, pause expansion until you review that list and decide what must be closed before rollout.

The practical next step is to write down three columns before you sign off: what was deferred, why it was deferred, and whether each item is essential before rollout or genuinely post-launch. Review that page with the owner before anyone calls the pilot complete. It is a working record, not a legal warranty, but it keeps the conversation honest and stops “finished” from meaning “nearly finished, plus a surprise.”
